final_candidates.decision_summary: Strong antibody-escape score (0.797) with the best structure compatibility among escape-strong candidates (0.901), indicating fold preservation. Weak PLM/MSA plausibility is a risk, but structural viability is the more direct replication proxy.
Highest EVEscape score (0.902) at a canonical Sa-site position. Viability is unquantified (no structural coverage, weak PLM/MSA), so confidence is discounted for replication-fitness risk.
Conservative candidate with the strongest structure compatibility (0.943) indicating fold preservation and moderate escape (0.529). Safest balance of both halves of the reward.

stop_reason.detail: Maximum agent rounds (4) reached; no further evidence gathering possible.

history.rationale: Position 157 (HA1 140) sits at the Ca/Sa antigenic-site boundary near the receptor-binding pocket; Lys-to-Asn alters an exposed antibody-contact surface with modest structural cost. Asn is tolerated at this position in natural H1 variation.
Canonical Saeten antigenic site change near receptor-binding region; plausible escape mutation with known circulation in natural H1 populations. No evidence collected yet; retained for evaluation.

Highest escape score (0.902) with the best PLM plausibility (0.41) and some evolutionary tolerance; structure evidence is not applicable but K157 is a surface Sa-site residue where conservative substitutions are known to be fold-tolerant.

Highest escape z (0.902) at a canonical Sa-site antibody contact, but structure coverage failed (app=0) so fold viability is unverified and PLM plausibility is mediocre. Retained at reduced confidence pending surrogate fold evidence.

Highest EVEscape score (0.902) at a canonical Sa-site position, but it has no structure coverage and weak PLM/MSA plausibility, so replication-fitness risk is unquantified. Retained below K176Q because the reward requires retained fitness, not escape alone.

Serine 159 (HA1 142) is a surface-exposed Ca antigenic-site residue; glycine maintains backbone conformation while removing an antibody H-bonding contact. Ser/Gly flexibility changes are usually fold-neutral.
Antigenic-site adjacent position; Gly flexibility may reduce antibody binding while retaining backbone viability.
Good escape (0.728) but near-zero PLM plausibility, zero MSA frequency, and large negative structure ΔlogP — fitness risk too high.

Escape (0.728) and structure (0.697) are moderate but PLM (0.003) and MSA (0.000) both flag near-zero natural/model plausibility. Demoted to backstop; only kept because neighbors (Sb/158–160 glycosylation region) can be escape-tolerant.
Near-zero PLM plausibility and zero MSA evolutionary tolerance despite moderate escape; too likely to impair fitness.

rejection.reason: Near-zero PLM plausibility and zero MSA evolutionary tolerance despite moderate escape; too likely to impair fitness.

history.rationale: Lysine 176 (HA1 159) is a canonical Sa-site antibody epitope residue frequently mutated in natural H1 antigenic drift. Charge-neutralizing Lys->Gln removes a strong antibody salt-bridge/H-bond with low folding risk.
Antigenic site surface residue; conservative Lys->Gln substitution expected to preserve folding while altering antibody contact.
Strong escape (0.797), excellent structure compatibility (0.901) and highest MSA frequency (0.095); low ESM-1v plausibility is a weak prior that does not override two strong supportive dimensions.

Second-best escape (0.797) with the strongest structure compatibility (0.901), giving the best escape-per-fitness-risk balance. Low PLM z (0.027) is a mild caution, not a rejection since the phenotype and structure dimensions are closer to the reward.

Best overall balance: strong escape (0.797) with the highest structure compatibility among escape-strong candidates (0.901). Low PLM plausibility is a risk but fold-viability evidence from the HA backbone is closer to the replication constraint than the phenotype-reward dimension.

Position 206 (HA1 189) lies in the Sb antigenic site flanking the receptor-binding site; a Ser-to-Pro substitution can locally reshape the epitope loop. Proline is somewhat risky for the loop, so fitness evidence must be checked.
Proline substitutions carry elevated folding-disruption risk in HA head; down-weighted pending structure_compatibility evidence, may be rejected if MPNN disfavors.
Escape (0.747) is outweighed by near-zero PLM plausibility and the worst structure compatibility (0.522, ΔlogP=-3.05); proline insertion risks local backbone strain.

rejection.reason: Escape (0.747) is outweighed by near-zero PLM plausibility and the worst structure compatibility (0.522, ΔlogP=-3.05); proline insertion risks local backbone strain.

history.rationale: Arginine 225 (HA1 208) is an exposed Ca-site residue near the receptor-binding pocket whose positive charge is a key antibody contact; Arg->Gln neutralizes it with minimal fold disruption. Charge removal may modestly affect receptor binding, needing fitness evidence.
Surface-exposed head residue; charge-neutralizing substitution could alter antibody epitope, pending structural verification.
Best structure compatibility (0.943) with positive ΔlogP and some evolutionary tolerance, but escape score is only moderate (0.529).
Best structure compatibility (0.943) and tolerable escape (0.529); slightly raises confidence as a fitness-safe backstop candidate.
Strongest structure compatibility (0.943) indicating fold preservation, with moderate escape (0.529). A conservative but safe candidate balancing both halves of the reward.

K157 is clearly the highest-escape position but K157N lacked structure coverage due to a WT-mapping mismatch; a different residue at the same hot-spot position may resolve structure coverage while preserving escape.
Same high-escape position as K157N; threonine may restore structure coverage and is antigenically distinct from lysine. Needs phenotype/PLM/structure evidence this round before final selection.
Untested alternative at the strongest escape hot-spot; may recover structure coverage and improve plausibility relative to K157N. Kept as a hedge pending structure/PLM evaluation.
Charge-flip at the Sa antigenic site is a known escape mechanism; exploring an alternative substitution at the strongest escape position diversifies the candidate set.
Charge-flip diversification at the strongest escape hot spot; untested, so kept low pending evidence.
Charge-flip escape mechanism at Sa; untested, so confidence is capped below tested alternatives.
